passages.context: Exact project-created editorial-projection passage for the Roman-1962 easter-vigil Litany of the Saints, first part.
passages.locus: easter-vigil, Litany of the Saints, first part; editorial-projection artifact physical lines 1-19; antecedent 1922 Tours Mame, printed pp. 264-266 (running head Sabbato Sancto), artifact PDF pp. 378-380, READ ON THE PAGE IMAGES at 400 dpi. The Mame prints the litany undivided; its first 45 printed lines carry exactly the 48 invocations of the 1962's first part, and the invocation that follows them on printed p. 266 is Propitius esto - the very point at which the 1962 divides. Corroborated in the tracked 1862 text layer, printed pp. 208-210 (folio markers 208 at line 36441, 209 at 36552, 210 at 36698), litany running lines 36464-36746, where Genitrix stands at 36504, 18 Sancte lines at 36506-36557 and 12 Omnes lines at 36509-36574.; target printed pp. 198-199, no. 991; artifact PDF pp. 279-280. The part ends where the rubric at no. 18 says it does, usque ad invocationem Propitius esto: its last invocation is Omnes Sancti et Sanctae Dei, intercedite pro nobis, and printed p. 200 begins DE BENEDICTIONE AQUAE BAPTISMALIS. (Both earlier lanes gave the range as printed pp. 198-205; that is wrong - 200 onward is the blessing of the font.)

passages.context: Exact project-created editorial-projection passage for the Roman-1962 easter-vigil Litany of the Saints, second part.
passages.locus: easter-vigil, Litany of the Saints, second part; editorial-projection artifact physical lines 21-41; antecedent 1922 Tours Mame, printed pp. 266-267 (running head Sabbato Sancto), artifact PDF pp. 380-381, READ ON THE PAGE IMAGES at 400 dpi. Its Propitius esto follows Omnes Sancti et Sanctae Dei with no break at all, and its litany ends with the same three Agnus Dei, the same Christe audi nos / Christe exaudi nos, and the same rubric handing over to the Mass's Kyrie. Corroborated in the tracked 1862 text layer, printed pp. 208-210, lines 36585-36746 (libera lines 36601-36625, domnum 36650, nosmetipsos 36674, Agnus 36714, closing Kyrie 36746).; target printed pp. 210-211, no. 1000; artifact PDF pp. 291-292. The rubric that introduces it, DE ALTERA PARTE LITANIARUM no. 27, stands on printed p. 209 (PDF p. 290), but no invocation does; the part itself begins at no. 1000 on printed p. 210 and ends with Christe, exaudi nos on printed p. 211, immediately before the heading TEMPUS PASCHATIS. The Kyrie that follows belongs to the Mass, not to the litany (rubric 1 on printed p. 211).

passages.rights_basis: Triptych created the bounded selection, transcription layout, normalization decisions, and collation record and offers those editorial contributions under CC BY 4.0. The underlying Latin prayers are public domain in the United States because the separately registered Pustet printing was published at Ratisbon in 1862. Triptych claims no exclusive right in those underlying words. The target-edition comparison selects only mechanical punctuation, project orthography, and the conclusion as printed, within the preexisting formulas; no page image, layout, rubric, marginal number, or other 1962-only matter is reproduced.

work.description: A project-created editorial source projection containing bounded Latin prayer bodies in date-specific artifacts. It is neither an edition of a historical hand missal nor an edition of the Missale Romanum. Each artifact records the transformation rule over separate public-domain antecedent and 1962 page-image witnesses; its passages let consumers cite the projected bodies without assigning Triptych's target-controlled collation choices to the antecedent printing.
